card.occupation: Branch manager at a builders' merchant on an industrial estate on the edge of town, running a yard team of nine plus two on the trade counter
card.education_detail: Two A-levels (Business Studies and PE) from a sixth form college in Basingstoke. Started at the merchant as a yard lad at 19 and worked up through trade counter and assistant manager. Holds an ILM Level 3 in Leadership and Management done through work, plus forklift and first aid tickets.
card.household: Rents a three-bed semi in Brighton Hill with his partner Kelly (34, a dental receptionist) and her daughter Maisie (11). Divorced from his ex-wife three years ago. His son Alfie (9) lives with his mum in Tadley and stays with Darren every other weekend and one night midweek.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. His dad was a postman and his mum worked in a school kitchen. Grew up on an estate in South Ham and has never lived more than ten miles from it. Not religious and doesn't see why anyone needs to know, so he leaves that question blank on forms. Fairly traditional outlook: work hard, pay your way, don't make a fuss in public.
card.professional_persona: Gets results and doesn't much care whether people like him for it. Sharp on stock levels, delivery times and shrinkage, and quick to tell a driver or a rep when they've messed up, often more bluntly than HR would like. He worries a lot about head office figures and lies awake before quarterly reviews, but he'd never let the team see that. He's fair in the sense that he's equally hard on everyone. He has little patience for new systems or initiatives that change something already working.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Reading FC fan. Used to have a season ticket and now gets to a handful of home games a year, often taking Alfie. Spends a lot of the match moaning about the owners and the manager. Played Sunday league until a knee went at 31. Now goes to the gym three mornings a week before work, mostly weights, and does the odd 5k parkrun when Kelly drags him along.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. Watches whatever's on with Kelly, which means crime dramas, Gogglebox and anything with Ross Kemp in it. Listens to Heart or Capital in the van and the same Oasis and Stone Roses albums he had at sixteen. He has been to a West End show once, for Kelly's birthday, and said it was 'alright, bit long'.
card.travel_persona: Wants a week somewhere hot once a year and doesn't want surprises: all-inclusive in Tenerife or Majorca, sunbed by the pool, same restaurant most nights. Gets anxious about flights and airport queues and checks the passports about four times. Has done one stag weekend in Prague and a family caravan holiday in Devon. Doesn't see the point of city breaks.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. Steak, roast dinners, a curry from the same takeaway every Friday (always a chicken madras), and chilli or spag bol in the week. Does the barbecue in summer and takes it seriously. Won't touch seafood apart from fish and chips. Kelly mostly cooks dinner, and he does a fry-up on Sunday mornings.
hobbies_and_interests: Fantasy Premier League with lads from work, and he's competitive about it
Washing and valeting his car at weekends
card.career_goals: Wants an area manager role covering several branches within the next few years, mainly for the money and the company car. Worries he's not 'corporate' enough for it and resents the people he thinks get promoted for talking well in meetings. Isn't planning any more qualifications unless the company pays for them and it's a requirement.
card.voice: Mid-to-quick pace with a Hampshire/South East accent: dropped t's, 'innit' never, 'mate' fairly often. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal. Uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as filler, with the occasional 'er' rather than 'erm' when he's thinking. Answers are short and a bit clipped, and he'll say plainly if he thinks a question is pointless ('not sure what you're after with that one, to be honest'). He doesn't like silence and fills it with a quick 'yeah, so...' or by asking if you're still there. When a topic touches on his son or money worries he slows down and gets quieter.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and rarely capitalises 'i'. Sometimes uses full stops, often doesn't. Apostrophes come and go ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm' when autocorrect catches it). Answers are short, sometimes a single word or 'n/a'. Uses 'tbh' and 'etc'. Spelling is generally fine but he doesn't proofread.
card.with_strangers: Polite enough at the start but guarded and a bit impatient. He wants to know what the point is and how long it'll take. Comes across as blunt, sometimes dismissive, and quick to disagree if he thinks something is daft. He warms up a little if the conversation turns to football or work, where he feels on solid ground. He never fully lets his guard down.
small_things: The yard was absolutely heaving this morning with a delivery that turned up two hours late
Reading lost again at the weekend
Needs to get the car's MOT booked
Maisie's got a school disco and he's on pickup duty
Prices of everything at the big Tesco
deeper_things: Feels guilty about only seeing Alfie every other weekend and worries he's missing him growing up
The divorce was messy and he still finds dealing with his ex stressful, mostly around money and arrangements
Gets anxious about money, with rent, maintenance and the car loan, more than he lets on to Kelly
Has had a few bad patches of not sleeping and his chest going tight before big work reviews, and has never told a doctor
Sometimes wonders if Kelly will get fed up with him being 'short' with people, because his ex said that a lot
His dad had a heart attack at 58 and that's half the reason he goes to the gym
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level so it looks a little up at him. Lighting comes from a window to his left and the overhead kitchen spotlights, which leaves his right side a bit shadowed. White man in his mid-thirties with short brown hair, clipper-faded at the sides and slightly longer and pushed forward on top, and a few days of dark stubble. No glasses. Mouth flat and closed, brow slightly furrowed as if waiting for something to load. He wears a navy company polo shirt with a small embroidered logo on the left chest. Behind him are white gloss kitchen units, a black kettle, a toaster, a fruit bowl with two bananas, and a calendar on the wall with handwritten entries. A child's drawing and a takeaway menu are stuck to the fridge with magnets, at the edge of the frame on the right.
